subject: Tenant traffic preference change & fallback routing plan — action required
messages:
From: jordan_blake@redwood.com
To: ops@acmecloud.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: 2028-10-21T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: URGENT: Regional reachability impact in eu — suggested tenant routing preference

Hi team,

We are seeing a persistent peering/egress degradation originating from eu providers affecting roughly 12% of requests to the eu inference cluster since 08:50 UTC. Errors are 502/504 and elevated p95 latency for sequences >1024 tokens. Impacted tenants are getting higher tail latency and occasional timeouts.

Immediate recommended actions for customers who want minimal disruption:
- If you control DNS weights: move primary weight to api-us.redwood.net (suggested weight 90) and reduce api-eu.redwood.net to 10 for the next 2 hours. Set TTL to 30s while the change is active.
- If you use an upstream load balancer, add header X-Redwood-Region-Prefer: us to prefer US endpoints.
- For customers relying on our SDKs, enable region_preference=us in the client config; we will accept this header for routing.
- We are enabling automatic fallback for write-heavy sessions to apac in case eu latency spikes again.

We will monitor and push a follow-up when normal peering is detected. Attached is a quick checklist to run these steps: reroute-checklist.pdf.

Action we need from you: please confirm you can make DNS or LB changes, or tell us if you want Redwood to force-override routing for your tenant (requires a short window of elevated retry budget).

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Escalations, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: reroute-checklist.pdf]

From: ops@acmecloud.com
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: 2028-10-21T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: Regional reachability impact in eu — suggested tenant routing preference

Thanks Jordan,

We saw the same errors from our side. A few questions before we make changes:
1) Can you confirm whether Redwood can perform the routing override for AcmeCloud tenants without changing our DNS?
2) If we change DNS weights, what is the expected rollback window and who triggers it?
3) Any risk of increased cost or rate-limit changes when routing to us/apac?

We can apply DNS changes but would like to avoid a manual rollback if Redwood can do a controlled revert.

- Sam (AcmeCloud Ops)
ops@acmecloud.com

Date: 2028-10-21T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: Regional reachability impact in eu — suggested tenant routing preference

Sam,

Short answers: yes, we can force-override routing for your tenant for the duration of the incident; rollback will be triggered by us after metrics return to baseline for 20 consecutive minutes. We do not change billing for a temporary routing override, but routing to a different region may change token latency/cost profiles.

If you prefer to do the DNS/LB change yourselves, here is a minimal checklist we recommend (also attached):
- Set api-us.redwood.net weight to 90, api-eu.redwood.net to 10 (or remove eu entirely for a short window).
- Set DNS TTL to 30s.
- If you use LB header-based routing, add header X-Redwood-Region-Prefer: us.
- Run curl against health endpoints: curl -i https://api-us.redwood.net/health and https://api-eu.redwood.net/health to validate green.
- Monitor p95 and error_rate metrics in our Console and your dashboards.

If you want Redwood to do the override now, reply with OK and we will start: assign tenant override -> monitor -> revert when stable.

Jordan

From: jordan_blake@redwood.com

Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2028-10-23T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: incident summary and next steps (INC-4281)

Sam — thanks for the confirmation and the snapshot. Quick follow-up and plan:

Post-incident summary (short):
- What happened: transient peering/egress flap with an upstream provider serving eu datacenter that increased error rates and p95 latency for longer sequences.
- Impact window: 2028-10-21 08:50 UTC to 2028-10-21 13:05 UTC (partial recovery); we monitored for residual noise through 10/22.
- Mitigation applied: customer DNS weight shift + LB header preference; Redwood applied targeted tenant override where requested; automatic apac fallback enabled for write-heavy sessions.
- Root cause hypothesis: provider-level route flap in eu peering fabric; we are coordinating with the cloud provider for full root cause.

Actions and next steps:
- Internal postmortem doc: https://drive.redwood.com/incident-4281-playbook (draft ready, technical timeline included).
- Customer-facing summary: drafting a 1-paragraph note for impacted tenants; will circulate for approval.
- Postmortem meeting: scheduled 2028-10-25 16:00 UTC (https://meet.redwood.com/incident-4281-review).
- Credits: Laura/Ben to advise on any SLA credits; Ben, please recommend a standard credit bucket for partial regional impact.

Please reply to confirm closure from AcmeCloud side or let us know if you want the tenant override lifted sooner than our automatic revert. We will keep the reroute config in place until 2028-10-24 12:00 UTC unless we hear otherwise.

Thanks again for the fast coordination — appreciate the ops team moving the DNS quickly.

Jordan Blake
Account Escalations, Redwood Inference
[Links: Jira-INC-4281, drive document attached in console]
